Welcome toThorntree Primary SchooL
At Thorntree we pride ourselves on being a happy and friendly school where our staff and pupils enjoy strong and respectful relationships and everyone is welcomed and valued.
We have a positive relationship with our parents and carers. We pride ourselves in our good relationship with all stakeholders.
We are a good school with a rich curriculum and our children enjoy learning here. We have aspirations for all of our children, we want them to leave us as well-rounded citizens who have been encouraged to fulfil their full potential, always aiming high.

Promoting British Values in Our School
We actively promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
At Thorntree School we actively promote these values in every aspect of school life.
The British value of Democracy
At the beginning of each year classes make a plan that outlines the rights and responsibilities of every member of the class.
Every class has two School Councillors. Interested candidates write a mini manifesto which they present to the class. A polling station is then set up in the hall for all children to cast their vote, instilling in the children an understanding of how citizens can influence decision making through the democratic process.
The School Council meets regularly and its role includes supporting the SLT in making decisions about school life, managing a small budget, gathering opinions of the children in their class, fund raising and suggesting and implementing ways in which school life can be improved for all children.
Democracy is taught during assemblies, circle times and PSHE sessions. Children regularly get opportunities to express their views in school through Pupil Voice interviews and questionnaires.
The British value of the Rule of Law
Children at Thorntree are taught to follow the rules they have helped to set in their class.
They also follow whole school rules and the playground rules that were devised by the School Council. All parents sign a home/school agreement that outlines the rights and responsibilities of children, parents and staff at our school.
School policies reflect our ethos of inclusivity and diversity and ensure that processes are clear and fairly administered.
Children are taught why we need rules to govern us in and out of school. Teachers explain that with rules come responsibilities and consequences for when rules are broken. The Positive Behaviour Policy at Thorntree is regularly reviewed and amended to ensure that there is a failsafe system in place to ensure all children feel safe, happy and able to thrive at Thorntree.
The school uses a restorative approach to managing behaviour, which is often more effective in resolving an issue than simply imposing a sanction.
Behaviour at Thorntree is good and the children are a credit to the school when they partake in school trips and learning away from the school.
The British Value of Individual Liberty
Freedom of speech is actively encouraged at Thorntree and children are taught how to voice their own views whilst showing respect for the views of others.
Children regularly showcase their opinions, beliefs and cultures.
Our robust anti bullying policy ensures that any reported issues of bullying are dealt with quickly and stringently.
We aim to provide pupils with the digital skills necessary to become independent learners. We promote the safe and age appropriate use of technology through a highly important E-safety curriculum where children are constantly reminded of the risks involved in using social media sites.
The British Value of Respect and Tolerance
At Thorntree, mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs underpins our ethos and values as does the understanding that everyone is different and that these differences should be celebrated.
Children are taught about respect for different cultures and beliefs through our RE curriculum, assemblies and special school events such as our yearly Carol Concert at the local church.
Visits to places of worship feature highly in our RE curriculum and are mapped out across the year groups to include each of the main world religions.
As a highly inclusive school, we understand and celebrate that all children learn in different ways and need different strategies and resources to support their learning. We foster a culture of understanding in each class so that children feel safe to use the methods and resources they need to help them learn best.
We ensure that when historical figures and people of scientific importance are studied, men and women from a variety of ethnic backgrounds are included.
Children’s work is valued and displayed to a high standard in the classroom and around the school. Children are praised for their efforts as well as their achievements.

pageCache.text:
Values and Ethos
Thorntree is a one-form entry, popular and successful community school situated in Charlton in the London Borough of Greenwich. It is a welcoming and friendly school where staff work hard to make children’s learning both relevant and enjoyable.
The school opened in 1927 as an Infant and Nursery School. In 1995 an extension was built to accommodate the older primary children. By 1998 Thorntree School was a fully-fledged Primary School catering for children aged three to eleven.
In addition to the classrooms we have a well-stocked library and two halls. Adjacent to Maryon Wilson Park, our hilly grounds contain woodlands, a large terraced field, a pond and three playgrounds. Almost hidden in a deep valley of trees, the school’s rural setting is rare for an inner- London school and gives it a special character.
Mission Statement (Ethos)
Thorntree is a forward-thinking inclusive school with high expectations for all our children. Here we embrace diversity, creative positive energy and promote achievement.
Thorntree is a place where everyone strives to be the best that they can be.
School Drivers
Our four school drivers are Creativity, Inquisitiveness, Healthy Minds and Healthy Bodies, and Our Environment. Please see the Curriculum Section of the website (under the heading 'Teaching and Learning') to read about them in more detail.
We are a Dyslexia Friendly school
We are committed to being a Dyslexia Friendly School. The school celebrates children’s strengths and encourages an ethos where children are accepting of each others' differences.
We recognise that it is the responsibility of every teacher and LSA within the school to remove barriers to learning and make learning accessible to all. Every child has an entitlement to have their needs met through Quality First Teaching and appropriate differentiation.
Classrooms have Dyslexia Friendly resources and displays and children are encouraged to recognise their own learning styles.
Our Values
Our School Values are listed below. These permeate everything that we do here at Thorntree:
O Ownership of learning
W Well-being for our bodies and minds
L Love of learning (life long)
A Appreciation of self and others
R Respect for diversity

What is the PE and School Sport Premium?
The PE and Sport Premium is designed to help children get an active start in life, supporting primary schools to improve the quality of their PE and sport provision so that pupils experience the benefits of regular exercise – from becoming healthier both mentally and physically to improved behaviour and better academic achievement. The funding is a ring-fenced grant for English primary schools to provide additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of PE, sport and physical activity. Allocations to schools are determined by a formula based on pupil numbers. The average one-form entry primary school will receive roughly £18,000 per year.
At Thorntree we use the Sports Premium in a variety of manners to improve our sports provision. Depending on current needs, this may include: specialist sports or dance teachers; swimming & cricket lessons; sports equipment; sports club subsidies; costs of joining in with local competitions and events; staff CPD and training in this area. All after school clubs are offered to Pupil Premium children at a reduced price.

Community Connections
Thorntree plays an active apart in the local community:
Local Parks Thorntree has an excellent working relationship with our local Park Rangers. Our Early Years classes pay regular visits to our three neighbouring parks and our Junior Sports Days are also held in one of our local parks.
Charlton Athletic Football Club Being its closest primary school, Thorntree has strong links with Charlton Athletic.
Local Churches. Thorntree Primary School has very strong links with local churches St Thomas' Church and St Lukes' Church. We make regular visits to these churches and do workshops about festivals, and our annual Junior Carol Concert is held at St Thomas'.
Trips to local locations All year groups at Thorntree have regular trips out into the local community, covering a huge variety of destinations: the National Maritime Museum, the Old Royal Naval College, the Ecology Park on Greenwich Peninsula, local places of worship of all denominations, local parks, Charlton House, Charlton Library, Woolwich Town Hall, the Heritage Centre, the Thames Barrier, and many more.
School Travel Plan We regularly take part in National Walk to School Week events and are regularly joined by the Local Authority Road Safety Officers.
School Council visit the Town Hall in Woolwich.
Harvest Produce Deliveries All of the produce donated at our Harvest Festival is delivered by Year 6 children to local elderly residents and foodbanks.
Summer Fayre and Summer BBQ Our Summer Fayre and the Summer BBQ have grown over the years and are now very well attended events open to everyone in the community.
After School Club Our After School Club is open to any local children aged 4-11 years old.
Charities We Regularly Support include:

The Royal British Legion (Poppy Appeal)
Save the Children (Christmas jumper day)
Comic Relief (Red Nose Day)

Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club is led by our own staff and operates from 8.00am to 8.55am every school morning.
Breakfast is provided and consists of a variety of cereals, toast, jam, marmalade, fruit, juice and water.
The Breakfast Club costs £4.50 per session per child. Payment should be made either in advance or on the day. Payments can be made online via School Money (contact the Office).
Drop-in sessions are available.
In all cases, should you wish your child to attend the breakfast club then please contact the school Office and fill in an application form.
All monies raised so far from the Breakfast Club have been used to purchase the adventure playground equipment (the Trim Trail) located on the field... which the children enjoy enormously. Any profit goes to the school fund and is used for extra resources for the classrooms.

Governors
The Governing Body of a school is a formal, legal entity which has certain areas of responsibility.
The Governing Body has a general responsibility for the conduct of the school with a view to promoting high standards of educational achievement including:
setting targets for pupil achievement
managing the school's finances
making sure the curriculum is balanced and broadly based
reviewing staff performance and pay
ensuring the safeguarding of all children and staff
The Governing Body delivers these responsibilities collectively through the action of the governing body as a whole, through committees (smaller groups of governors which focus on particular areas) and occasionally by individual governors. The Full Governing Body will usually meet once each term and will discuss issues affecting the school as a whole. The full governing body hears reports from committees on their individual areas of responsibility. At Thorntree we have main three committees:
Curriculum and School Improvement Committee
Finance and Personnel Committee
Premises and Health and Safety Committee
and also a Pay Committee and a Pay Appeals Committee

Pupil Voice
The School Council
The School Council at Thorntree gives pupils the opportunity to make a positive contribution to the school community. It gives the children their first taste of active citizenship and broadens their horizons beyond their individual classes through inter-class discussions and problem-solving.
The School Council meets regularly and is made up of democratically elected pupils from each class. In the School Council meetings, the school councillors represent the views of their own classes and then report back to their classes on the outcomes. It is a forum that enables the sharing of issues and ideas that need to be addressed as a whole school. Not only does it give the children ownership of some of the issues that affect them, it also helps them to develop as individuals.
The School Council have worked on developing the playground and outdoor areas as well as running their own stall at the Christmas Fayre to raise funds for the playground.
Class Ambassadors
Class Ambassadors are children who represent their classes when we have outside visitors. They talk to both visitors and Governors about the school and the work they have been involved in, for example themes, history/science topics, class texts, etc. They are able to signpost visitors to areas of interest in their class and around the school.
Junior Travel Ambassadors
Junior Travel Ambassadors are representatives from Year 5 and Year 6 who help others within the school to learn about sustainability and to keep themselves safe on the roads. They run competitions and talk about road safety in assemblies and the classrooms. They raise awareness among children and their parents/carers about the need to park safely when parking near the school. They take an active part in the annual Road Safety Week.
Year 6 Responsibility Roles
In Year 6, the children are encouraged to take on more responsibility. Each term, different Year 6 children take charge of re-cycling within the school. Some take charge of delivering milk and fruit to classrooms. Other Year 6 children take on the role of corridor monitors at the end of playtimes, helping the lower years to get back to their classrooms sensibly and promptly. Some become play leaders, promoting healthy activities at break times and making sure that everyone has someone to play with. Some pupils set out benches and chairs before assemblies and others play the music and assist with technology.
